transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you here?

Well, um, I guess what really made me come in is... I just can't shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are tracking my buys. Which is a lot to keep track of because I deal with so many vendors. Like this one guy who supplies our seasonal stuff, he drives this bright orange pickup truck that is just insanely loud. You can literally hear it vibrating the glass in the front office before he even parks. I used to want a truck exactly like that back in high school, but gas is just way too expensive now, you know? I don't know how anyone affords to fill up a tank that size. 

But anyway, yeah, they're... they're messing with the launch numbers. I know they are. They're doing it on purpose to make me look stupid. And my supervisor keeps pulling me into his office to show me these reports, saying the data doesn't prove anything. His office always smells like stale coffee and peppermint, it's really distracting, and he uses this ancient spreadsheet program that looks like it's from 1998. But yeah, he says the reports don't show it, but I just... I can't shake the feeling. So that's why I'm here.
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I mean... there have been plenty of weeks where I sleep maybe, I don't know, three or four hours? And I wake up just feeling completely wired and ready. Like, lying in bed just feels like a massive waste of time when I could be using that time to make moves. Which, honestly, is why I started looking into trading crypto late at night a while back. You can watch the overseas markets open, and it's a whole different vibe. 

My buddy Steve got really into it too, but then he dropped his phone in the lake on a fishing trip and got completely locked out of his digital wallet. We were up at this lake, about two hours north of here, and the mosquitoes were just absolutely huge up there. Like, the size of quarters. You'd smack one and it would actually leave a mark on your arm. I tried using that natural bug spray, you know, the citronella stuff? Total scam, doesn't work at all. It just makes you smell like a giant candle. But yeah... what were we talking about? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, three or four hours and I'm totally good to go.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being inserted into your mind or controlled by someone else?

No, I don't really think anyone's putting thoughts in my head. I mean, my thoughts are my own, they just... they go pretty fast sometimes. But no one's controlling them. If someone could control thoughts, they'd probably make everyone buy the same stuff, right? Which would actually make my job as a buyer so much easier. You wouldn't have to guess what the trends are gonna be for next quarter. Like right now, everyone is suddenly obsessed with these insulated stainless steel water bottles. The ones with the little straw lids? We literally cannot keep them in stock. 

I had to put in three separate emergency orders last week alone just to keep the shelves full. And the shipping delays on them are insane right now because they're all coming out of this one port on the West Coast that's having some kind of labor dispute. Or maybe it was a crane issue? I saw a documentary about those massive cargo ships once, and the amount of fuel they burn is just staggering. It's like thousands of gallons an hour. I don't even know how the ocean survives all that exhaust. But yeah, no, my thoughts are definitely just mine.
Have you had these suspicious beliefs even when you were not feeling unusually energized or needing much less sleep?

Yeah, actually... even when things slow down. Like, there was this stretch a while back where I was sleeping totally normal, maybe seven or eight hours a night, and I didn't feel like I was, you know, running the whole market or whatever. I was just feeling pretty calm. But I still spent a few weeks absolutely convinced that they were tracking my buys. And... and I was still hearing that voice back in the stockroom. 

Our stockroom is a total nightmare, by the way. The lighting back there is awful, they use these cheap fluorescent tubes that flicker constantly and give you a massive headache if you're back there for more than ten minutes. I told maintenance about it like three times, but the guy who runs maintenance, Jerry, he's always busy fixing the HVAC system. Our AC unit is from, like, the Stone Age. It makes this horrible clanking sound every time it kicks on. Reminds me of my grandpa's old tractor. He had this farm out in Ohio, grew soybeans mostly. I used to go out there in the summers when I was a kid. You wouldn't believe how hot it gets in the middle of a soybean field in July. The humidity just hangs there like a wet blanket. We used to catch fireflies in mason jars... but yeah, even when I was feeling totally calm and sleeping fine, I still knew they were tracking my numbers and I was still hearing that voice.
How long have you been hearing that voice?

Well, I guess... the suspicious stuff and the voice, it's been going on for roughly ten months now. Yeah, about ten months. Which is crazy because ten months ago was right around the time I bought my new car. It's a Honda Civic, but I got the sport trim because I really liked the alloy wheels. They look so much sleeker than the standard ones. I had to wait three weeks for it to be delivered to the dealership, though, because apparently there's still a microchip shortage or something? That's what the salesman told me, anyway. His name was Greg. Nice guy, but he kept trying to upsell me on this extended warranty package that covered, like, fabric protection for the seats. I told him I don't even eat in my car, so why would I need fabric protection? I mean, unless you're driving around with a bunch of kids spilling juice boxes everywhere, it just seems like a way for them to squeeze an extra five hundred bucks out of you. My sister has three kids, and her minivan is basically a rolling dumpster. You literally step on crushed cheerios every time you get in. I told her she needs to get it detailed, but she says there's no point until they're all in middle school. But yeah, ten months. It's been about ten months since all that started.
During any of these periods, did you ever feel unusually euphoric or irritable?

Yeah, definitely. I get these stretches where I feel like the whole city is just... opening up for me, you know? Like I'm completely dialed in, and everything is clicking. I'll feel amazing, just on top of the world. But then, if someone questions a purchase order I put in, or tells me to slow down, I snap way harder than I mean to. I just get so irritable. Like last week, my manager asked why I ordered so many of those reusable silicone food storage bags, and I practically bit his head off. 

Which is ridiculous, because those bags are actually a great seller. People are trying to move away from single-use plastics, which makes total sense. Have you seen the pictures of the Great Pacific Garbage Patch? It's terrifying. Just this massive swirling vortex of plastic bottles and grocery bags and fishing nets out in the middle of the ocean. I read an article that said it's twice the size of Texas now. How do you even clean something like that up? They have these ships with giant nets trying to scoop it out, but it feels like using a teaspoon to empty a swimming pool. My buddy Dave went deep-sea fishing off the coast of Florida last year and said he saw a sea turtle that had a plastic ring from a six-pack stuck around its shell. He managed to cut it off, but still. It makes you really think about where all our trash goes. I try to recycle everything now, but half the time I feel like the recycling truck just dumps it all in the same landfill anyway. But yeah, when I'm feeling that good, if anyone gets in my way or tells me to slow down, I get incredibly snappy with them.
Have you ever gone for at least two weeks at a time when your mood was not unusually high, low, or irritable, but you were still hearing the voice or believing people were tracking you?

Yeah, I think I already mentioned that, right? Like, there was that stretch where things were just... normal. I was sleeping fine, not feeling like I was running the market or anything, just feeling pretty calm. But I still spent a few weeks absolutely convinced they were tracking my buys, and I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom. 

Speaking of the stockroom, I really need to get some new boots if I'm gonna keep working back there. The concrete floors are just brutal on your arches. My buddy Mark, he works construction, and he told me I need to invest in some Red Wings. He swears by them. Says they take like a month to break in, and you'll get blisters the size of quarters, but after that, they mold to your feet like slippers. He's been doing framing for, like, five years now. Building these massive custom homes out in the suburbs. The crazy part is the price of lumber right now. He said a sheet of plywood is triple what it used to be. I don't know how anyone affords to build a house these days. It's like you need to win the lottery just to get a two-bedroom ranch. I buy a scratch-off every Tuesday, just for fun, you know? Never win more than five bucks, though. But yeah, to answer your question, even during that calmer stretch for a few weeks, I was still hearing the voice and knowing they were tracking me.
Have there ever been any weeks-long periods when your mood was so high or irritable that it caused major problems at work, at home, or with other people?

Yeah, definitely. When I get like that, my job has taken a real hit. Like, I've missed buying deadlines because I'm just too focused on other things, and I've totally damaged some vendor relationships. I even made some really impulsive purchasing calls that got me formally warned by my supervisor. 

Which, honestly, supervisors can be so micromanaging sometimes. It's like, I get it, you have to watch the bottom line, but do you have to CC three different people on an email just to ask why I ordered an extra pallet of energy drinks? Energy drinks are huge right now anyway. Have you seen those new ones with the zero sugar and the crazy flavors? Like "Cosmic Stardust" or whatever? My buddy Kyle drinks like three of them a day. I keep telling him his heart is gonna explode. He's an electrician, so he's up at, like, 4 AM every day wiring these new apartment complexes. He says he needs the caffeine just to function. I tried one once and my hands were shaking so bad I could barely hold my phone. I don't know how he does it. He's always been kind of intense, though. We used to play in a volleyball league on the weekends, but I stopped showing up for that. I just pulled away from friends, you know? Stopped going to the gallery nights we used to hit up, too. Just haven't been feeling it. But yeah, the work stuff got pretty bad. I definitely got written up for those impulsive buys.
Have there been any times when the voice or the belief that people were tracking you kept going while you were also having a clearly manic episode?

Yeah, for sure. Like, there were those weeks where I was barely sleeping at all, just running on pure adrenaline, you know? I was talking nonstop to anyone who would listen about upcoming sneaker trends—which, by the way, the retro high-tops are making a huge comeback. I saw this one pair online that were, like, neon green and purple, total 90s vibe. Reminds me of when I was a kid and everyone had those pump sneakers. Did you ever have a pair of those? You'd literally pump up the tongue for a tighter fit. I always wanted a pair, but my mom said they were too expensive. She was always trying to find a deal, clipping coupons on Sunday mornings. The Sunday paper used to be so thick, remember? Now it's practically a pamphlet. My grandpa still gets the physical paper delivered every morning. He sits on his porch with his black coffee and reads the sports section. He's a huge baseball fan. Complains about the new pitch clock, though. Says it ruins the rhythm of the game. I don't really watch baseball, it's a little too slow for me. I prefer basketball. Fast-paced, lots of scoring. Anyway, during that time when I was feeling totally untouchable at work, I was also absolutely convinced that the vendors were manipulating the numbers on my orders. And yeah, I was definitely still hearing that voice in my head, just pushing me to move faster, buy more, go, go, go.
Have you ever had at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or feeling tracked, but you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

Yeah, I think I said that earlier, didn't I? Like, there was that chunk of time—maybe a few weeks—where things felt pretty calm. I was actually sleeping normally, not like that crazy stretch where I felt like I was running the whole market. I was just, you know, going to work, coming home. 

But my commute has been awful lately. They're doing all this construction on the interstate, adding an HOV lane or something, and it backs up traffic for miles. I end up sitting there listening to podcasts just to keep from losing my mind. Have you ever listened to any of those true crime ones? They're wild. I started this one about a guy who faked his own death to get out of debt. He bought a boat, sailed out, and just disappeared, leaving his wife with all these unpaid loans. People are crazy, right? Makes you wonder how well you really know anybody. Like my neighbor, Mrs. Gable. Sweetest old lady, brings my mail up to the porch if it's raining, but she has this massive collection of porcelain dolls that stare at you when you walk past her living room window. Gives me the creeps. I try not to look when I'm taking the trash out. Trash pickup is another thing—they keep changing the days. Used to be Wednesday, now it's Thursday, and if you forget, you're stuck with it for a whole week. 

But yeah, even when I was feeling calmer and sleeping fine for those few weeks, I was still totally believing that people were tracking my buys. And that voice was still there in the stockroom, just talking away.
Have there been any times when the voice or the belief that people were tracking you lasted for at least two weeks while you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

Yeah, like I was saying, there was definitely a time when things felt... I don't know, normal? Or at least calmer. I was actually sleeping, not staying up all night feeling like I was running the whole market. 

Which is a relief, because when you don't sleep, your skin gets so bad. Have you noticed that? Like, I started getting these weird breakouts on my chin, and I had to go to the drugstore and buy all these different face washes. They have an entire aisle now just for acne stuff. It's overwhelming. Salicylic acid, benzoyl peroxide... I stood there for like twenty minutes reading the backs of the bottles. The lighting in those stores is always so harsh, too. It's like fluorescent and buzzing. It always makes me feel like I'm in a hospital or something. Speaking of hospitals, my aunt had to go to one recently because she tripped over her golden retriever and broke her wrist. The dog is huge, like eighty pounds, and he just lays right in the middle of the hallway. She had to get pins put in and everything. She's doing physical therapy now, but she says it hurts like crazy. I feel bad for her, but I also told her she needs to train that dog better. He jumps on everybody. 

But yeah, even during that calmer stretch where I was sleeping fine and not feeling super hyped up, I still spent a few weeks totally believing people were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom, just going on and on. So yeah, it definitely happened without the crazy energy stuff.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when your mood was back to normal, but you were still hearing the voice or feeling like people were tracking you?

Yeah, I... I feel like we just talked about this, right? But yes. There was definitely that stretch, like a few weeks, where my mood was just... normal. Like I wasn't buzzing with all that energy, I was sleeping fine, not feeling like I was the king of the market or anything. 

It was actually around the time I bought this new mattress. Have you ever tried one of those memory foam ones that come rolled up in a box? It's crazy how they vacuum seal them. You cut the plastic and it just inflates like a life raft. I got the hybrid one, with the springs and the foam, because the all-foam ones sleep too hot. I read all these reviews online about how people were waking up sweating. And I hate being hot when I sleep. I keep my AC on like 68 degrees, even in the winter. My electric bill gets a little high, but it's worth it. The power company actually sent me this letter saying my usage was higher than my neighbors. Like, why are they comparing me to my neighbors? What if my neighbors are just really cheap and sit in the dark? It's kind of invasive if you think about it. They have these smart meters now that track exactly when you're using electricity. 

But anyway, yeah, even during that calmer time when I was sleeping on the new mattress and my mood was totally fine, I still spent a few weeks believing that people were tracking my buys at work. And that voice was still there in the stockroom, just talking to me. So the mood stuff was gone, but the other stuff was still happening.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest or pleasure in most things?

Depressed? No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really get sad or down like that, or lose interest in stuff. 

I actually have a lot of interests. Like, I've been getting really into restoring old cast iron skillets lately. You wouldn't believe what people just throw away or leave at thrift stores. I found this Griswold number eight pan from like the 1930s for five bucks at a yard sale. It was completely covered in rust, just orange all over. But if you soak it in a vinegar bath—half water, half white vinegar—it eats right through the rust. You have to be careful though, if you leave it too long, it'll pit the iron. Then you scrub it down to the bare metal and season it with grapeseed oil. A lot of people use flaxseed oil, but I read on this forum that flaxseed can flake off over time. Grapeseed has a higher smoke point. I bake it in the oven at 450 degrees for an hour, let it cool, and do it like three or four times. It gets this beautiful, glassy black finish. Nothing sticks to it. I made eggs on it yesterday, and they just slid right around like they were on ice. Eggs are getting so expensive though, have you noticed? I went to the store the other day and a dozen was almost six dollars. It's ridiculous. I was thinking about maybe getting a couple of chickens for the backyard, just to have my own eggs. But then you have to build a coop, and worry about raccoons getting in...

So, yeah, no, I haven't really had any times where I felt super depressed or anything like that.
Have there been any times when the voice or the belief that people were tracking you lasted for at least two weeks while you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

I feel like you keep asking me the same thing, Doc. But yeah, like I said, there was definitely a time when I was calmer. I was sleeping normally, not feeling like I was running the whole market. 

Which was nice, because when I'm sleeping better, I actually have time to make breakfast. I started making those eggs in the cast iron skillet I told you about. I even tried making a frittata the other day. You whisk the eggs, throw in whatever vegetables you have in the fridge—I used spinach and some bell peppers that were about to go bad. You start it on the stove and then finish it in the oven. The trick is to not overcook it, or it gets all rubbery. My mom used to make eggs like that, just cooked to death. She’d serve them with this really dry toast. She always bought that cheap wheat bread that tastes like cardboard. I don't know why she didn't just buy a nice sourdough. Sourdough is so much better for your gut, anyway. I watched a whole documentary about fermentation and how the bacteria in sourdough actually pre-digests the gluten for you. It's fascinating. People have been making bread that way for thousands of years, and now we just buy this processed stuff in plastic bags. 

But anyway, yeah, even during that calmer stretch where I was sleeping and not feeling all hyped up, I still spent a few weeks totally believing people were tracking my buys at work. And I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom. So yes, it happened even when I wasn't having all that crazy energy.
Have there ever been times when the voice or the belief that people were tracking you happened only while you were having mania, and never when your mood was normal?

Well, like I was saying, there were definitely times when it was all happening at once. Like, during those weeks when I was barely sleeping, just buzzing, you know? I was talking nonstop about sneaker trends to anyone who would listen. I felt totally untouchable at work, like I could predict exactly what was gonna sell out before it even dropped. And during that same time, I was also completely convinced that the vendors were manipulating the numbers on me. And I was hearing that voice, too, pushing me to move faster, buy more. 

Sneaker culture is wild right now, by the way. Have you seen what people are paying for vintage Jordans? It's like an alternative stock market. I was looking at this pair of 1985 Chicago Jordan 1s online the other night. The leather quality back then was just different, you know? They used thicker cuts. Now everything feels so plasticky and synthetic. It's because they mass-produce them in these huge factories overseas to cut costs. My buddy tried to tell me that the new releases are more comfortable because of the updated foam technology, but I don't care about the foam. It's about the history. The silhouette. I actually thought about starting a side hustle where I clean and restore old sneakers. You just need a good suede eraser, some specialized brushes, and this cleaning solution that foams up. You have to be really gentle on the suede though, or you'll ruin the nap. If you brush it too hard, it gets all stiff and crusty. It's kind of like restoring that cast iron I was talking about, it takes patience. 

But yeah, anyway, to answer your question, those things definitely happened together—the voice, the tracking stuff, and the crazy high energy where I felt like a god at work. But like I said before, the tracking and the voice also happened when my mood was totally normal. So it wasn't *only* when I was hyped up.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believing people were tracking you, but you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

Yeah, I think I just said that, right? Like, there was definitely a time when I was just normal. I was sleeping fine, not having all that crazy energy, not feeling like I was running the whole market. But I still spent a few weeks totally believing people were tracking my buys at work. And I was still hearing that voice in the stockroom. 

It's so weird being in the stockroom when it's quiet like that. The fluorescent lights in there always have this low hum, you know? It drives me nuts if I focus on it too much. My uncle used to be an electrician, and he told me that hum is because of the magnetic ballast in the older light fixtures vibrating. They're supposed to phase those out for electronic ballasts, which are way quieter and more energy-efficient. I tried to tell the store manager we should upgrade them because it would save on the electric bill in the long run, but he didn't want to hear it. He's always cutting corners. Like with the breakroom coffee—he switched from the good dark roast to this cheap generic brand that tastes like burnt dirt. I can't even drink it anymore. I started bringing my own cold brew from home. It's actually really easy to make, you just need a coarse grind and you let it steep in the fridge for like 16 hours. It's way smoother than hot brewed coffee. 

But yeah, to answer your question again, yes. Even when I was having a calmer stretch and sleeping normally, the tracking stuff and the voice were still happening for a few weeks.
Have you ever had at least one full week of hearing the voice or believing people were tracking you while your mood was completely normal and you were not manic?

Doc, are you messing with me right now? I feel like I'm stuck on a loop here. Yes, a few weeks is more than one week. So like I just said, even during that calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys. And hearing the voice in the stockroom. 

I don't know how many different ways I can say it. It's honestly like dealing with the freight dispatchers at work. You send them the routing guide, and they still call you asking where to send the truck. They use this completely outdated software from like 2004. I keep telling management we need to migrate to a cloud-based system, but nobody listens because they don't want to pay the monthly licensing fees. Which is stupid, because we lose so much money on chargebacks when shipments are late. Last month, we had a whole pallet of retro high-tops just sitting on a loading dock in Newark because someone smeared the shipping label. 

They really need to switch everything to RFID tags instead of standard barcodes. With RFID, you don't even need a line of sight to scan the box, the radio waves just pick it up instantly. They use them a lot in marathon races to track the runners' times. Have you ever run a marathon? I feel like it would completely destroy your knees. Human bodies aren't really meant to run on asphalt for 26 miles straight, you know? Our ancestors ran on dirt and grass. 

But yeah, anyway... what were we saying? Right, the week thing. Yes. To answer your question again, yes. It happened for a few weeks when my mood was totally normal.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest or pleasure in most things?

Depressed? No, not really. I don't think I've ever had a time where I just lost interest in everything for a couple of weeks. I'm always pretty locked in on my stuff. 

Like, you can't really afford to lose interest in the sneaker market anyway, it moves way too fast. If you stop paying attention for even a few days, you miss a whole release cycle. Like last month when they shock-dropped those Travis Scotts. People were losing their minds. The SNKRS app crashed for like twenty minutes. That app is notoriously terrible, honestly. They use this algorithmic draw system that's supposed to stop bots from buying up all the stock, but the bot developers are always one step ahead. They use residential proxies to make it look like the traffic is coming from regular home IP addresses instead of data centers. It's basically an arms race. 

My buddy pays like two hundred bucks a month just to rent a server in Virginia so his ping time to the servers is faster by a few milliseconds. Milliseconds! It's exactly like high-frequency trading on Wall Street. I watched this documentary on how they laid a straight fiber-optic cable through mountains just to shave off like three milliseconds of trade time between Chicago and New York. Imagine spending hundreds of millions of dollars just to be slightly faster at buying stocks. The drillers had to go through solid limestone to make the tunnels. Limestone is super porous, though, so they kept running into underground water pockets, which completely messed up their drill bits. 

But yeah, wait, what were you asking? Oh, depression. No, I don't get sad or lose interest like that.

patient.answer:
Well, um, I guess what really made me come in is... I just can't shake this feeling that people at work, and even some of the vendors, are tracking my buys. Which is a lot to keep track of because I deal with so many vendors. Like this one guy who supplies our seasonal stuff, he drives this bright orange pickup truck that is just insanely loud. You can literally hear it vibrating the glass in the front office before he even parks. I used to want a truck exactly like that back in high school, but gas is just way too expensive now, you know? I don't know how anyone affords to fill up a tank that size. 

But anyway, yeah, they're... they're messing with the launch numbers. I know they are. They're doing it on purpose to make me look stupid. And my supervisor keeps pulling me into his office to show me these reports, saying the data doesn't prove anything. His office always smells like stale coffee and peppermint, it's really distracting, and he uses this ancient spreadsheet program that looks like it's from 1998. But yeah, he says the reports don't show it, but I just... I can't shake the feeling. So that's why I'm here.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there is a history of a prior manic or hypomanic episode, which would support a schizoaffective or bipolar-spectrum diagnosis over schizophrenia.

target_item.name: Decreased_Sleep

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean... there have been plenty of weeks where I sleep maybe, I don't know, three or four hours? And I wake up just feeling completely wired and ready. Like, lying in bed just feels like a massive waste of time when I could be using that time to make moves. Which, honestly, is why I started looking into trading crypto late at night a while back. You can watch the overseas markets open, and it's a whole different vibe. 

My buddy Steve got really into it too, but then he dropped his phone in the lake on a fishing trip and got completely locked out of his digital wallet. We were up at this lake, about two hours north of here, and the mosquitoes were just absolutely huge up there. Like, the size of quarters. You'd smack one and it would actually leave a mark on your arm. I tried using that natural bug spray, you know, the citronella stuff? Total scam, doesn't work at all. It just makes you smell like a giant candle. But yeah... what were we talking about? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, three or four hours and I'm totally good to go.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has psychotic symptoms in the form of thought insertion/broadcasting or external control, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from bipolar disorder with psychotic features or a delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being inserted into your mind or controlled by someone else?

patient.answer:
Depressed? No, not really. I don't think I've ever had a time where I just lost interest in everything for a couple of weeks. I'm always pretty locked in on my stuff. 

Like, you can't really afford to lose interest in the sneaker market anyway, it moves way too fast. If you stop paying attention for even a few days, you miss a whole release cycle. Like last month when they shock-dropped those Travis Scotts. People were losing their minds. The SNKRS app crashed for like twenty minutes. That app is notoriously terrible, honestly. They use this algorithmic draw system that's supposed to stop bots from buying up all the stock, but the bot developers are always one step ahead. They use residential proxies to make it look like the traffic is coming from regular home IP addresses instead of data centers. It's basically an arms race. 

My buddy pays like two hundred bucks a month just to rent a server in Virginia so his ping time to the servers is faster by a few milliseconds. Milliseconds! It's exactly like high-frequency trading on Wall Street. I watched this documentary on how they laid a straight fiber-optic cable through mountains just to shave off like three milliseconds of trade time between Chicago and New York. Imagine spending hundreds of millions of dollars just to be slightly faster at buying stocks. The drillers had to go through solid limestone to make the tunnels. Limestone is super porous, though, so they kept running into underground water pockets, which completely messed up their drill bits. 

But yeah, wait, what were you asking? Oh, depression. No, I don't get sad or lose interest like that.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview and elicit the patient's chief complaint in their own words.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you here?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a 10-month history of psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions and auditory hallucinations) that clearly persist for at least several weeks during euthymic, non-manic periods, which establishes psychosis independent of mood episodes. He also has recurrent manic episodes with decreased need for sleep, elevated/expansive mood, irritability, pressured speech, increased goal-directed activity, impulsive spending, and functional impairment at work. Because psychosis occurs for a sustained period outside mood episodes, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type is favored over bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
